links.outcome: Factuality score gain from abstaining on high-uncertainty generated radiology reports
links.effect: Abstaining from high-uncertainty reports improved factuality scores by 10%, achieved by rejecting 20% of reports (Radialog, MIMIC-CXR).
links.quote: By abstaining from high-uncertainty reports, our approach improves factuality scores by 10%, achieved by rejecting 20% of reports using the Radialog model on the MIMIC-CXR dataset.

links.outcome: Ability of sentence-level uncertainty to flag the lowest-precision sentence in each report
links.effect: Sentence-level uncertainty flags the lowest-precision sentence in each report with an 82.9% success rate.
links.quote: Furthermore, sentence-level uncertainty flags the lowestprecision sentence in each report with an 82.9% success rate.

unlisted_practices: Black-box semantic consistency-based uncertainty quantification at report and sentence level for radiology report generation, requiring no model access or logits

screen.practice: uncertainty-based abstention and sentence-level flagging of generated reports
screen.reason: Evaluates a plug-and-play semantic consistency uncertainty quantification framework to filter out/abstain from hallucinated radiology reports and flag low-precision sentences, testing an output-filtering/safeguard deployment practice on benchmark data.

primary.practice: uncertainty quantification and selective abstention / output filtering
